text:
Olivia: Trying to onboard candela-3b for production. Running AWQ and GPTQ bakeoffs. Hitting weird kernel errors on Triton with CUDA12 images, and AWQ seems to mismatch kernels sometimes. Anyone run into this?

Raj: What errors are you seeing? logs? :thinking:

Olivia: Paste of the tail of the server log:
```
triton: ERROR Loader::loadModel failed: cuBLAS status CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED
RuntimeError: cuBLAS failed to create handle: CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED
During call to attention_cuda::half2_attention
```
Also Triton falls back to CPU for some layers and latency doubles.

infra-bot: Note: node gpu-agg-12 reports NVIDIA driver 535.86, CUDA runtime 12.1. Container image: rwinf/cuda12-triton:latest

Anya: On vLLM side I saw similar: "half2 kernel not found" when the model was quantized with AWQ's per-channel scale. vLLM expects FP16/FP32 kernels unless you supply custom kernels or TensorRT-LLM.

Mike: For TensorRT-LLM the build we use needs --use-cublaslt and TRT 9.x. CUDA12 + cublaslt mismatches can cause CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED. Try rebuilding tensorrt-llm with CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12 and link against cublasLt from the same toolkit.

Jordan: Quick bakeoff numbers for candela-3b (eval on LAMBADA / story-completion):
- FP16 baseline: perplexity 9.8, exact-match 48.2%
- AWQ int8 (per-channel, 4-bit prefs for heads): perplexity 10.1 (+3%), exact-match 47.6% (-0.6%)
- GPTQ (autogptq default): perplexity 10.9 (+11%), exact-match 45.9% (-2.3%)
So AWQ is closer to baseline on quality, but driver/runtime issues are happening more with AWQ artifacts.

Raj: Thanks. Can you share the quant config you used? I want to reproduce across nodes.

Olivia: Config I used (simplified):
```
quantizer: awq
bits: 8
group_size: 128
per_channel: true
quant_mode: inference
```
Server startup: `python -m rwinf.triton.server --model-dir models/candela-3b --backend tensorrt-llm`

Sara: Short-term workaround: run AWQ inference on CUDA11 container where Triton/TensorRT used in our validated matrix. Docker run: `docker run --gpus all -e CUDA_VERSION=11.8 rwinf/rt-deps:11.8 /bin/bash` and mount model. Not ideal but isolates the driver mismatch.

Anya: Also note that vLLM's fused attention kernels will error on quantized weights unless you convert attention weights to a supported layout. We added a small rewriter in the AWQ pipeline that pads head dims to multiples of 8 to avoid some kernels failing.

Mike: If you want to try TensorRT-LLM path, try this minimal repro: `trtexec --onnx=candela.onnx --minShapes=input:1x1 --maxShapes=input:1x1024 --fp16` — if trtexec fails with CUBLAS errors, it's the same underlying cublas/cudart mismatch.

Olivia: Follow-up: I reran on a cuda11 image and Triton + TensorRT-LLM started fine, AWQ latency looks acceptable. But on CUDA12 some nodes still succeed and some fail — suspect driver ABI changes across kernels.

Jordan: Also observed that AWQ+Triton path sometimes uses a different kernel name: `fused_attn_v2` vs `fused_attn_v3` depending on sequence length heuristic — that explains intermittent behavior.

Raj: I'll spin a 6-node matrix across cuda11/12, driver 525/535, triton 2.20/2.21, vllm main/tags and report. If reproducible, we file infra ticket to pin validated images.

Sara: Can someone open a short ops doc for fallback policy? If Triton falls back to CPU we should surface that in Console per-route and warn about 2x latency.

Olivia: Will do. Punting to a short action list: 1) Raj reproduce, 2) Jordan collect detailed eval diffs, 3) Mike try rebuild of tensorrt-llm against CUDA12, 4) Sara add Console alert for CPU fallback.

deploy-bot: Created issue ML-784: "candela-3b AWQ/GPTQ bakeoff: CUDA12 + Triton kernel incompatibility" and attached latest logs.

Raj: I'll update ML-784 with matrix results later today. Thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
